findings.title: The player-facing floor claims mix up the 2.28 policy with what the loader needs: the release .so needs only GLIBC_2.17
findings.failure_scenario: Several statements give the wrong picture of what happens below glibc 2.28. README:67 says 'A Linux library needs the glibc it was linked against, or a newer one'. README:74 says 'On an older system the dynamic loader refuses the library, so the LuaJIT CPU is not offered there'. roadmap:219 says 'On an older glibc, System.load fails'. jit-guide:80 says 'a .so needs the glibc it was linked against'. jit-guide:1110 says 'the .so's floor is its build host's'. roadmap:204 says the .so 'must come from a glibc 2.28 host'. But the release .so is linked on 2.28 and needs at most GLIBC_2.17. On glibc 2.17-2.27 (CentOS 7, Debian 9, Ubuntu 18.04) the loader would accept it [I]. A player or server admin on such a system is told the LuaJIT CPU cannot appear, when it probably will, untested and unsupported. A support answer could also blame glibc for an unrelated load failure. The distro list itself is correct: RHEL, Alma and Rocky 8 and Debian 10 ship 2.28, and Ubuntu 20.04 ships 2.31.
findings.evidence: [M] readelf -V -W on dist .so 6c888050: the highest GLIBC needs are 2.12, 2.14 and 2.17. roadmap:231 itself records 'logs glibc: highest version needed GLIBC_2.17', and jit-guide's 7.7 table says 'at most GLIBC_2.17'. NEEDED are libm.so.6, libpthread.so.0, libc.so.6 and ld-linux-x86-64.so.2, all present on older glibc systems [S].
findings.fix: Present 2.28 as the supported floor that gradle enforces, not as the point where loading stops. For example: 'The release .so may need at most GLIBC_2.28 (gradle refuses more), so it loads on any x86_64 Linux with glibc 2.28 or newer: <list>. Today's needs at most GLIBC_2.17, so it may also load on older systems, untested and unsupported; where glibc lacks a version it needs, the loader refuses it and the LuaJIT CPU is not offered.' Reword 'needs the glibc it was linked against' as 'needs, at most, the glibc it was linked against', and 'the floor is the build host's' as 'the build host's glibc caps the floor'.

findings.title: git_head's git path can return an enclosing repository's commit, so the new commit refusal passes a wrong fingerprint commit
findings.failure_scenario: OCLJ_LUAJIT is a LuaJIT tree with no .git of its own (a source export or a copy) inside another git work tree. The default path prototype/watchdog/luajit is inside OC-LuaJIT's work tree; the path is gitignored, but git still walks up from it. With git on PATH, `git -C "$1" rev-parse HEAD` walks up and returns OC-LuaJIT's HEAD, so ERIS_LJ_COMMIT silently names this repository's commit and changes with every commit of it. Without git, the same tree is refused. The same happens when the nested .git is broken, because git skips it and keeps walking up. It also happens when GIT_DIR is exported, as git does for hooks (githooks(5)), because GIT_DIR overrides -C. So the comment's invariant at :531-536 ('the two ways must never disagree') is false, and the refusal at :554 can be bypassed with a wrong value. The default nested checkout is answered correctly.
findings.evidence: [M] C:/Users/astro/claude-tmp/oclj/glibc/review/review-build/gh-win.out (git_head text extracted from the repo file, Git for Windows 2.55). real checkout: git [1ee778a4], no git [1ee778a4], git --short=8 [1ee778a4]. A tree with no .git inside a scratch repo: git [55abd184] (the scratch repo's HEAD), no git []. A nested broken .git: git [55abd184], no git []. A linked worktree (.git is a file): git [55abd184], no git [] (a refusal, which is loud and acceptable). gh-win-gitdir.txt: with GIT_DIR=<scratch>/.git exported, git_head on the real LuaJIT checkout returns [55abd184]. [M] Alma git 2.43.7, run as uid 1000, reads the real checkout as 1ee778a4 both with -C and with --git-dir. [S] The error at :554-557 says 'no git on PATH' even when git is present and the checkout's .git is a worktree file.
findings.fix: Point git at the checkout's own .git, never discovery or the environment: `gh_h=$(git --git-dir="$1/.git" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null) || gh_h=`. --git-dir accepts a 'gitdir:' file, so worktrees and submodules still resolve with git. Tested in scratch (fn-fixed.sh, gh-win-fixed.out): real checkout [1ee778a4] both ways; worktree git [55abd184]; tree with no .git and broken nested .git [] both ways (refused); with GIT_DIR exported [1ee778a4]. verdicts.title: 'The .so imports no dl* symbol' is literally false: it imports dl_iterate_phdr
verdicts.evidence: [M] In AlmaLinux 8, readelf --dyn-syms -W on dist 6c888050 and on alma-2's 62555188 lists UND dl_iterate_phdr@GLIBC_2.2.5 (probe script review/verify-docs/probe.sh). The claim appears in jit-guide.md:1106 ('the .so imports no `dl*` symbol [M]'), roadmap.md:220 ('the .so imports no `dl*` symbol [M, `nm -D`]') and native/build-native.sh:285-286 ('(the .so imports no dl* symbol)'). [I] dl_iterate_phdr comes from libgcc's unwinder (-static-libgcc) and lives in libc: libdl.so.2 is not NEEDED, and the --no-undefined link succeeded without -ldl. verdicts.title: git_head's git path can return an enclosing repository's commit, so the new commit refusal passes a wrong fingerprint commit
verdicts.evidence:
[S] native/build-native.sh:538 `gh_h=$(git -C "$1" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null) || gh_h=`. git discovers the repository from "$1" upward, and it obeys an exported GIT_DIR. The refusal at :554 only tests that the value is non-empty, and nothing compares LJ_COMMIT with the 1ee778a4 pin (grep of build-native.sh). HEAD's code (`git -C ... rev-parse --short=8 HEAD || echo unknown`) walked up in the same way, so this is not a regression. What is new is the claim at :531-536 that the two ways 'must never disagree', and the refusal that this case gets past.
[M] C:/Users/astro/claude-tmp/oclj/glibc/review/verify-build/gh-win.out (Git for Windows 2.55) and gh-alma.out (AlmaLinux 8, git 2.43.7, uid 1000). The script, verify-gh.sh, extracts git_head from the repo file without editing it. Results in both:
- The real checkout gives git/nogit/fixed = 1ee778a4.
- `$REPO/native/luajit`, a repository directory with no .git of its own, gives git [3adfeaf7], which is OC-LuaJIT's own HEAD. nogit gives [] (refused).
- A tree with no .git inside a scratch repo gives the scratch repo's HEAD with git, and [] without it.
- The real checkout with GIT_DIR=<scratch>/.git exported gives the scratch HEAD.
- A relative GIT_DIR=.git happens to resolve correctly.
The case is reachable only with a non-default OCLJ_LUAJIT: a tarball or copy with no .git inside a git work tree. The default prototype/watchdog/luajit has its own .git and reads correctly. Low.
verdicts.fix:
At build-native.sh:538, read the checkout's own .git and never use discovery or the environment: `gh_h=$(git --git-dir="$1/.git" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null) || gh_h=`. [M] The fixed variant in gh-win.out and gh-alma.out was tested on both hosts:
- real checkout: 1ee778a4
- repository directory without .git, and copy without .git: [] (refused)
- linked worktree, whose .git is a gitdir: file: still resolves
- exported foreign GIT_DIR: 1ee778a4
Optionally reword :555 to 'git could not read it, and there is no readable .git/HEAD', since git may be present.

verdicts.title: PREREQUISITES 7 and the docs still say a build without git writes "unknown" into the fingerprint; the code now reads .git/HEAD or refuses
verdicts.evidence:
[S] build-native.sh:537-557. git_head falls back to .git/HEAD, a loose ref or packed-refs, and `[ -n "$LJ_COMMIT" ] || fail` refuses an empty commit, so 'unknown' cannot reach ERIS_LJ_COMMIT any more. Only the JNLUA log line keeps `${JNLUA_COMMIT:-unknown}` (:560), and that is display text.
[S] Each of the following states the old behaviour as current fact:
- build-native.sh:2051-2054: 'where git is missing or refuses the tree, the fingerprint says "unknown"'. It is new this round; HEAD's build-native.sh has no such text (git show HEAD: grep).
- docs/roadmap.md:196, Status 2026-10-19, added this round: 'build-native.sh:526 reads LJ_COMMIT with git -C ... rev-parse, or writes unknown ... every .so built there stamps unknown'. The cite :526 is now the comment header; LJ_COMMIT is at :553.
- docs/roadmap.md:238: an open 'decision for the user' that rests on the same premise.
- docs/jit-guide.md:1117: 'AlmaLinux 8 has no git, so its builds stamp unknown ... [M]'.
[M] gh-alma.out: Alma now has git 2.43.7 and reads the checkout as 1ee778a4, and the no-git path on the real checkout also gives 1ee778a4 (gh-win.out, gh-alma.out). The bench run's own ff-linux.sh header confirms that the user installed git on 2026-10-19.
Nothing is computed wrongly, and the build's own refusal message is accurate. But two authoritative docs and the script's setup header misstate how the release .so's fingerprint behaves, and they put a decision to the user that the code has already settled.
verdicts.fix:
Rewrite build-native.sh:2051-2054 to say what the code does. The commit comes from git, or from .git/HEAD when git cannot run (a detached hash, a loose ref or a packed-refs line). With neither, the build fails, so a native never stamps 'unknown'. Blobs move only between natives that agree on that commit (eris_lj.c refuses a differing fingerprint).
In roadmap.md:196, add the resolution to the 2026-10-19 status: git_head with the fallback and the refusal, and git now installed in Alma. Move the cite to :553.
Mark roadmap.md:238 item 1 as resolved, or reword it.
Delete the 'stamp unknown' sentence at jit-guide.md:1117, or rewrite it to describe the fallback and the refusal.

verdicts.title: Two small false statements in the new build-native.sh comments: the unversioned .so 'does not load', and the .so 'imports no dl* symbol'
verdicts.evidence:
[M] C:/Users/astro/claude-tmp/oclj/glibc/review/verify-build/elf-facts-alma.out (AlmaLinux 8.10, readelf 2.30):
- The oldlink .so (md5 bf0d0916): the six pthread imports are unversioned R_X86_64_JUMP_SLOT relocations, there is no FLAGS/BIND_NOW entry, and NEEDED is libm, libc and ld-linux, with no libpthread.
- The release-style alma-2 additive .so (md5 62555188): it imports `dl_iterate_phdr@GLIBC_2.2.5` as a GLOBAL FUNC UND, so 'imports no dl* symbol' (:285-286) is literally false. The point that nothing needs libdl is still right, since NEEDED has no libdl.
[M] lazyload-alma.out: lazyload.c, linked without -pthread, has libpthread 'not loaded' before each dlopen.
- oldlink .so: RTLD_LAZY gives 'loaded', rc=0. RTLD_NOW gives 'undefined symbol: pthread_sigmask', rc=1.
- alma-2 .so (control): loads under both modes, and libpthread is then loaded.
So :1895-1897 ('does not load in a host without libpthread') holds only for an eager load or `ldd -r`. A lazy load succeeds and fails later, at the first unresolved call. [S] lj52shim.c:2126: that first call in the watchdog start is pthread_condattr_setclock, not pthread_create as the proposed fix wording says. [I] HotSpot's os::dll_load uses RTLD_LAZY. In practice no JVM lacks libpthread, and neither statement changes what the gate decides.
verdicts.fix:
At :1895-1897, say: 'and in a host without libpthread the same .so loads lazily, then exits with "symbol lookup error: ... undefined symbol" at the watchdog's first pthread call (pthread_condattr_setclock, lj52shim.c:2126). An eager load fails at once (RTLD_NOW and ldd -r name them; ldd -d names none).'
At :285-286, say: 'it imports nothing from libdl (no dlopen, dlsym, dlclose or dlerror; its one dl* import, dl_iterate_phdr, is libc's, from libgcc_eh)'.

verdicts.title: OCLJ_* overrides set on the Git Bash side never reach full-linux.sh, so a negative-control arm run that way is really the product and still scores 82/0
verdicts.evidence: [M] My own probe, C:/Users/astro/claude-tmp/oclj/glibc/review/verify-harness/env/probe-env.sh, output in env/out.txt. These two forms gave OCLJ_DISPOSE=<unset> in AlmaLinux-8: `OCLJ_DISPOSE=off OCLJ_PERSIST_BUNDLE=off OCLJ_SMOKE=/x MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl.exe -d AlmaLinux-8 -- sh probe-env.sh`, and the same after `export`. Ubuntu with the prefix form also gave <unset>. Two forms did reach the script: `wsl.exe -d AlmaLinux-8 -- env OCLJ_DISPOSE=off sh ...` and `WSLENV=OCLJ_DISPOSE:$WSLENV`. [S] full-linux.sh:8-9 shows only the Git Bash invocation. Lines :15, :29 and :30-31 then say OCLJ_JAVA overrides, that OCLJ_TIMEOUT may be set, and that the other variables are 'passed through when set', and none of them says the variables must be set inside the distro. smoke-test.sh:646 defaults OCLJ_DISPOSE to on. Give the working form, `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl.exe -d AlmaLinux-8 -- env OCLJ_DISPOSE=off sh /mnt/c/.../full-linux.sh ...`, or say to add the names to WSLENV. verdicts.title: chain-linux.sh reports an old run dir's exit and CHECKS as the new arm's result and writes env.txt into that old dir
verdicts.evidence: [M] Stub replay, C:/Users/astro/claude-tmp/oclj/glibc/review/verify-harness/chain/. I ran an unmodified copy of chain-linux.sh (md5 79e2323b, the same as the repo's) in AlmaLinux-8. Beside it was a stub full-linux.sh made of the real script's lines 1-42 plus a marker tail. Before the run I created all seven lx-*-t dirs, each with an old exit.txt=0 and a smoke.log reading 'CHECKS: 82 FAILURES: 0 OLD-RUN-<arm>', and moved the chain log aside. Each arm printed 'REFUSING: ... already exists' to stdout only, in chain.out, and the stub's marker was never written. Yet runs/chain-linux-t.txt logged every arm as 'lx-<arm> exit=0 SMOKE| CHECKS: 82 FAILURES: 0 OLD-RUN-lx-<arm>', and the chain then wrote env.txt into the OLD lx-disposeoff-t and lx-bundleoff-t dirs. [S] chain-linux.sh:32 refuses only when the LOG exists. full-linux.sh:42 exits 99 before refuse() is defined and writes nothing into RUN. It needs a log moved aside with the run dirs left in place, so it is reachable but unlikely. all.sh's runs dir sits under $G, which all.sh refuses to reuse (:26), so the running chain is not affected.
verdicts.fix: Put this first in one(): `[ -e "$RUNS/$name-$T" ] && { echo "$name REFUSED: $RUNS/$name-$T exists" >> "$LOG"; return; }`. Alternatively, before the first arm, refuse the whole chain if any $RUNS/lx-*-$T exists.
